subject: Follow-up: runtime log audit and confidentiality affirmation
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Follow-up: runtime log audit and confidentiality affirmation

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for your patience while we completed the technical review following the transient runtime issue on 2027-05-08. Below is a concise summary of our findings and the evidence we are delivering for your records.

Summary of findings
- No customer records were read or exfiltrated. We validated access patterns across the affected service and found no requests that matched customer table reads.
- The incident touched the model inference path only; affected traffic was isolated to ephemeral model prompts and cache keys.
- KV-prefix and in-memory caches were flushed within 2 minutes of mitigation and verified by subsequent sampling.
- For additional assurance, we engaged ForensicOps to run an independent hash reconciliation on relevant runtime artifacts. Their short report is attached.

Evidence delivered
- runtime-log-hash-20270508.csv: list of log files scanned with SHA256 hashes and byte counts.
- chain_of_custody_20270508.pdf: internal chain-of-custody that documents collection times and collectors.
- forensicops-summary-20270509.txt: third-party validation notes and reconciliation steps.

Technical details (high-level)
- Scope: three inference nodes in us-west-2 that processed queued requests between 01:02:12 and 01:09:00 UTC.
- Controls checked: IAM roles, instance-level permissions, kernel-level process boundaries, and object-store ACLs. No unexpected principals were observed.
- Verification steps: full log grep for customer table identifiers, cross-check of request signatures, hash-by-hash file comparison against previous retention copies.

Next steps and ask
- I attached the artifacts and uploaded them to a shared Drive folder (link below) for your compliance team. If you want a signed, notarized copy of the chain-of-custody, we can arrange that via ForensicOps.
- Please confirm if this level of evidence is sufficient for your audit, or if you need additional export formats (CSV -> Parquet, or raw JSON logs).

Link to evidence: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/Acme/incident-20270508-evidence

Apologies again for the disruption. We take confidentiality and integrity very seriously and are open to any follow-up requests.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Security Response Manager
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: runtime-log-hash-20270508.csv] [Attachment: chain_of_custody_20270508.pdf] [Attachment: forensicops-summary-20270509.txt]

From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@acme-payments.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bob Li <bob.li@acme-payments.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 18:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: runtime log audit and confidentiality affirmation

Connor —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the detail. A couple of quick follow-ups from our audit/compliance team:
- Can you provide the exact SHA256 hashes for the archived log bundles we have under retention (we need a per-file map to our archive IDs)?
- Would it be possible to get the chain-of-custody notarized (PDF with timestamp authority)?
- Who from your side can provide an attestation letter that no PII or payment tokens were accessible during the window? Our auditors prefer an explicit statement.

If you can send those items today that would be ideal. I copied Bob for procurement so he can track any formal paperwork.

Thanks,
Alice
Head of Security Operations
Acme Payments

On Sun, May 9, 2027 at 16:12 Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai> wrote:

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, ForensicOps Inc. <ops@forensicops.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: runtime log audit and confidentiality affirmation

Hi Alice —

Appreciate the questions. Quick responses and attached artifacts:

1) Per-file hashes: attached CSV (runtime-log-hash-20270508.csv) includes a column mapping internal retention ID -> file path -> SHA256 -> byte count. We generated the CSV from the immutable retention snapshot taken at 2027-05-08T01:11:00Z and cross-referenced against s3-retain-archival/Acme/2027-05-08.

2) Notarized chain-of-custody: ForensicOps performed timestamping for the collection baseline. We've attached chain_of_custody_20270508.pdf; the last page contains the RFC 3161 timestamp token and signer details. If you need a separate notarized (not cryptographic timestamp) signature, we can route that through our legal team.

3) Attestation letter: Below is an explicit attestation we can provide as a short-form letter on Redwood letterhead. If that works I'll create the signed PDF and route through Markus for executive sign-off.

--- attestation (draft) ---
Redwood Inference attests that, based on a full technical review of runtime artifacts and independent reconciliation conducted by ForensicOps Inc., there is no evidence that Acme Payments' customer records, PII, or payment tokens were accessed, exported, or exfiltrated during the 2027-05-08 incident window. The review covered all inference node logs, associated cache contents retained at collection time, and object-store transaction records for the affected timeframe.
--- end attestation ---

Please confirm if the draft attestation language meets your audit needs and we will issue a signed PDF.

Attachments: runtime-log-hash-20270508.csv, chain_of_custody_20270508.pdf, forensicops-summary-20270509.txt

Best,
Connor

[Attachment: runtime-log-hash-20270508.csv] [Attachment: chain_of_custody_20270508.pdf] [Attachment: forensicops-summary-20270509.txt]

Connor / Marissa —

This is exactly what we needed, thank you. The hash CSV maps cleanly to our own archive IDs and ForensicOps' summary answers our technical team questions. The draft attestation language is acceptable; please proceed with a signed PDF on Redwood letterhead. Procurement (copied) will follow up on any paperwork.

We consider this matter closed from our side pending the signed attestation. Appreciate the clear evidence and the third-party validation.

Regards,
Alice
